title: Sore the next day is not proof it worked. Here is what is
caption: Do you have to be sore for a workout to work? No: sore mostly means new, and the real proof is your reps going up and the stairs getting easier. Save this and count again in two weeks.

overlays.text: Nobody tells you this: sore the next day is not proof it worked.

scenes.footer: You have heard it. It is not true.

overlays.text: If you are not sore tomorrow, it did not count. That is the myth.

scenes.footer: A new move, a new angle, a first week.

overlays.text: Sore mostly means new. Not better, not harder. Just new to you.

scenes.footer: Less sore is not less work.

overlays.text: Do the same ten minutes every day. It stops feeling sore. It keeps working.

scenes.footer: You count it. Nobody else has to.

overlays.text: The proof is your reps going up and the stairs getting easier.

scenes.footer: Off the chair, no hands. Write the number down.

overlays.text: Sit-to-Stand. Count your reps in one minute today. Count again in two weeks.

scenes.footer: The number is yours. So is the strength.

overlays.text: Sore tomorrow or not, today's ten minutes counted. You built that.

scenes.footer: Save this and count again in two weeks.

overlays.text: How many did you get today?
